From your ground to the space station

Straight up to the station and its next pass. The clock moves, then goes back.

Open the trip: From your ground to the space station

Where you are standing

This is the ground you are standing on, seen from high above it. All the weather you have ever felt happens in the bottom twelve kilometres of air, a layer too thin to see from here.

The air, from the station's height

Space begins a hundred kilometres up, with nearly all of the air already below. From the station's height the air is the blue glow along the edge of the world.

The station, where it is this minute

The International Space Station, a laboratory and a home, about as long as a football pitch. It goes round the Earth sixteen times a day, eight kilometres every second.

The next time it crosses your sky

This is the station at the top of its next pass over you, with your ground below. From where you stand it looks like a bright star moving steadily across the sky, with no blinking lights.

Everything is drawn where it really is, from CelesTrak orbital elements and the planets’ own orbits (astronomy-engine).
